name: bite
description: Checks whether the "fixed" in your AI coding agent's commits is true. It takes each fix back out and runs your tests. Free, with no key.

readme.excerpt: [![GitHub Marketplace](https://img.shields.io/badge/Marketplace-Bite%20free%20check-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/bite-free-check) **Would your tests catch it if the bug came back?** Bite checks whether an AI coding agent's "fixed" is actually true. **Try it now.** It's free, needs no key, and never changes your files. If you have Python, paste these two lines into any terminal window (PowerShell, cmd, Terminal): ``` python -m pip install bite-check python -m bite_check --free ``` Outside a project, Bite first shows a demo on a tiny made-up one. To check your own project, type the second line and a space, drag your project's folder into the window (that types its path), and press Enter. Have [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io) or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)? One line does it, no install: `pipx run bite-check --free` or `uvx bite-check --free`. (On Linux or a Mac, if pip says "externally managed", use one of those.) If your commits never say "fix", add `--any` to check every recent change. To keep Bite installed as a `bite` command, see [Try it in a minute](#try-it-in-a-minute). **Here for Hack Week or your first open-source PR?** These [good first issues](https://github.com/connabyss/bite/labels/good%20first%20issue) are small, and each one says where to look and when it's done. Comment on one to claim it. ## Why you need this When an AI fixes a bug for you, it often says "Fixed, and I added a test." If you don't read code, you can't tell if that's true. A test is a tiny robot that checks one thing, like "2 + 2 should be 4", and shouts when it isn't. A good test shouts if the bug ever comes back. A weak one stays quiet no matter what. Bite checks your robots. It puts the old bug back on purpose and watches whether any test shouts. It's like testing a smoke alarm with real smoke instead of trusting the little green light. If a test shouts, that fix is guarded. If they all stay quiet, the next change, by you or your AI, could bring the bug back and nobody would notice. Bite names that fix, so you can tell your AI: "add a test that fails without this fix." ## How it works It takes each recent fix back out of your code and runs your tests. If they still pass, nothing guards that fix, and Bite tells you which one. That free check needs no key and works with pytest, npm test, cargo test, go test, dotnet test, Maven and Gradle (Java and Kotlin): ``` pipx install bite-check bite --free ``` With your own API key it goes one step further: it writes one small test of the commit's exact claim and runs it. That is how it found a memory leak in [prosemirror-py](#the-catch-that-shows-what-its-for) that a commit said it had fixed. > "Reverting the claimed fix and making the change prove itself under a real test is exactly the kind of check that > should exist for every "fixed" commit." > > — [Ivan Zdravkov](https://zdravkov.info), [on DEV](https://dev.to/izdravkov/comment/3jdej) ## Try it in a minute Install once with [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io), which gives Bite its own space so there's no venv to set up or activate: ``` python -m pip install --user pipx python -m pipx ensurepath ``` Close the terminal window and open a new one, then: ``` pipx install bite-check bite --demo ``` `bite --demo` builds a tiny made-up shop project in a temporary folder and runs the free check on it.
